Toyota Prius Buyer's Guide

From the 56-mpg Two Eco to the 220-hp plug-in, the Prius family covers more ground than its reputation suggests. Which one to buy used, and what to check.

By Diana Chambers · 5 chapters, about 20 min in all · Updated November 16, 2026 · Find one for sale

In this guide
  1. ●Overview
  2. 12017–2022
  3. 22023–2026
  4. 3Prime and Plug-in Hybrid
  5. 4Prius c and Prius v
  6. 5Used checklist

The Prius is the car that made hybrids ordinary in America, and between 2017 and 2026 Toyota sold it in 6 forms. The regular Prius covers 2 generations: the fourth generation, sold through 2022 and rated at up to 56 mpg, and the redesigned 2023 car, which went from 121 hp to 194 hp and is rated at up to 57 mpg. The plug-in Prius Prime could run 25 miles on electricity for 2017 and 44 miles for 2023, and Toyota renamed it the Prius Plug-in Hybrid for 2025. Toyota also ended 2 spinoffs in this period: the small Prius c after 2019 and the wagon-shaped Prius v after 2017.

For a used buyer, the choices are the generation, whether to plug in, and how much hybrid battery warranty is left. This guide has 5 chapters: one for each generation of the regular Prius, one for the plug-ins, one for the Prius c and Prius v, and the checklist to use before you buy.

Quick picks

  • Best all-rounder: a 2023 or later Prius LE, rated at 57 mpg combined, with 194 hp and 10 years of hybrid battery coverage.
  • Best value: a 2020–2022 Prius LE or XLE with records. Apple CarPlay is standard, and the hybrid battery is covered for 10 years or 150,000 miles.
  • Best for short commutes: a 2023 or later Prius Prime SE or Plug-in Hybrid SE, with up to 44 miles of electric range.
  • Best in snow: a 2019–2022 Prius AWD-e, or a 2023 or later Prius with all-wheel drive.
  • Most cargo space: a 2017 Prius v, with up to 67.3 cubic feet behind the front seats.
  • Think twice if you carry tall adults in the back. The 2023 Prius has less rear headroom than the car it replaced, and a 2017–2019 Prius Prime seats only 4.

The chapters

Chapter 1The Car That Made 50 MPG Normal2017–2022 · Fourth generation · Front drive or AWD-e

52 mpg as standard, 56 in the Eco grades, and automatic emergency braking on every one. The best-value used hybrid, if you can live with 10-second acceleration.

4 min readChapter 2The Prius People Turn to Look At2023–2026 · Fifth generation · Front drive or AWD

More than 3 seconds quicker to 60 than the old car, rated at up to 57 mpg, and genuinely good-looking. The catch is a tighter back seat.

4 min readChapter 3A Prius You Can Plug In2017–2026 · Prius Prime · Prius Plug-in Hybrid

Charge it at home and many commutes need no gas at all. Then it's still a Prius when the battery runs out. Which plug-in to buy, and whether it pays.

4 min readChapter 4The Small One and the Big One2017–2019 · Prius c · Prius v

One is the cheapest way into a Prius badge, the other carries almost as much as a small SUV. Both are discontinued, and both have quirks to know.

3 min readChapter 5Most Problems Hide in the Hybrid System2017–2026 · The used Prius checklist

The Prius has a reputation for lasting, and some have already covered big miles as commuter, fleet or rideshare cars. How to check the one in front of you, and the recalls to confirm.
